Thanks, interestingly that points out an endianness issue. Also see:

https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_NFLOG.html

The "NFULA_IFINDEX_OUTDEV" is clearly in Little-Endian in your file, but the dissector is always using Big Endian, which apparentyl is correct according to the linktype description there are the tcpdump site (all 32-byte quantities are supposed to be Big-Endian always.)

fsc?
This is header-only, I don't see how the FCS is relevant at all, and why it would be called a "no FCS" variant, instead of, say, `eth_header` or `eth_header_only`.
to fix

This doesn't work well. There's an `if (nflog_tree)` statement surrounding the switch statement where `hwheader.buffer` and `payload.buffer` are filled out, so this doesn't get properly called when there's no tree (i.e., when filtering).

So for example if I take your file and then filter for `eth.type = 0x0800` or any other of the Ethernet or IPv4 fields that visible in the tree, none of them will match.

See how these are *outside* the `if (nflog_tree)` block? That was so they would always occur, even with a NULL tree.

We could just get rid of the `if (nflog_tree)` test.

yes, it would be much simpler. then i dont get well what to pass as 1st param to

ti = proto_tree_add_bytes_format(nflog_tree, hf_nflog_tlv,
                             tvb, offset, tlv_len, NULL,
                             "TLV Type: %s (%u), Length: %u",
                             val_to_str_const(tlv_type, nflog_tlv_vals, "Unknown"),
                             tlv_type, tlv_len);

in case if nflog_tree == null. Simply tree fron params? Let me debug a bit. 
BTW how should i proceed if mr already merged?  Lets move to another one?

Yes, we'll need to make a new MR.

What we should do is just eliminate the `if (nflog_tree)` test and fix the block's indentation. All the various `proto_tree_add_item()` etc. API calls check if their first parameter is NULL and then return without doing to some of the expensive operations. You would still pass in `nflog_tree`, just not test it. (Testing for a null tree can speed things up in cases where operations outside the `proto_` API calls are expensive and don't need to be done with a NULL tree, e.g. calculating a checksum, but it's an optimization that can be difficult to do correctly.)

i added filter 'eth.type == 0x0800' and all items letf displayed. I really don't get in which case 
proto_field_is_referenced(tree, proto_nflog) will return false. Probably, for those input files which dont have nflog records at all. Or proto_field_is_referenced is not working anymore as expected

It's working as expected (well, as it always did, which is not necessarily what people expect), the problem is that you want to create your `payload` and `hwheader` *even if* the tree is null because no fields are referenced. If nothing is being filtered and no fields are referenced, `payload` and `hwheader` still need to be created so that the dissectors that they call are still called. That makes, e.g., the columns be filled out correctly when nothing is filtered.

On a capture I just took on Linux it is *NOT* Host Endian, unlike your file. This and other values are Big Endian, as specified here:
https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_NFLOG.html

~~In any case, `ENC_HOST_ENDIAN` would *never* be correct here. pcapng and pcap indicate the Endianness of the original host; that should be used, not the Endianness of the machine (a Little Endian box can read both L-E and B-E pcapng and pcap).~~ 

`ENC_HOST_ENDIAN` is for some very rare and unfortunate cases. For the TLVs and length, there's some handling in libwiretap specifically to swap the TLV type and length to host endian so for those two, but not the multi-octet integer field values, which are, according to the linktype description and when I just did a capture, always in Big Endian.

> move ip dissector inside NFULA_PAYLOAD, so we can see origin place of ip dissector

I personally don't like this change, but that's a matter of taste I suppose. I'd almost like a preference for the old behavior, although preference proliferation is a concern.
